character_vibe_description: Character & Vibe An honest snapshot - the energy, the people, the pace. The kind of thing no other directory tells you. Fort is where Mumbai's professional class comes to work. By 9am, the streets around the Bombay High Court are filled with lawyers in black coats. The corridors of the Reserve Bank of India hum with the quiet authority of monetary policy. The galleries of Kala Ghoda are being unlocked by curators. And the Irani cafés near Flora Fountain are serving their last round of morning chai to the commuters who have been coming here every day for thirty years. Fort is not a neighbourhood in the conventional sense - it is primarily a commercial and institutional district. But it has a residential soul too: the Parsi families who have lived in the same buildings since the 1930s, the advocates who have their chambers and their homes within walking distance of each other, and the artists and gallery owners who have made Kala Ghoda one of the most culturally alive precincts in Asia. Pin code 400001 is not just an address. It is a statement.

best_services.name: Institutions That Define India
best_services.description: Fort is home to institutions that define India's legal, financial and cultural life. The Bombay High Court - established in 1862 in a magnificent Victorian Gothic building - is one of the oldest and most respected courts in Asia. The Reserve Bank of India, headquartered in Fort since 1935, sets monetary policy for the world's most populous nation. The State Bank of India, HDFC, ICICI and virtually every major Indian and international bank have their head offices or flagship branches in Fort. The University of Mumbai's Fort campus, the Government Law College and the Asiatic Society Library have educated generations of India's finest minds. And the Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus - a UNESCO World Heritage Site - is one of the world's most magnificent railway stations, handling over 3 million commuters every day.

best_services.name: Kala Ghoda - Mumbai's Cultural Soul
best_services.description: Within Fort lies Kala Ghoda - Mumbai's premier art district and one of the most culturally alive precincts in Asia. Named after the black equestrian statue of King Edward VII that once stood here (now removed), Kala Ghoda is home to the Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Vastu Sangrahalaya (the Prince of Wales Museum), the Jehangir Art Gallery, the National Gallery of Modern Art and dozens of private galleries, design boutiques and cultural spaces. The annual Kala Ghoda Arts Festival - nine days of visual arts, music, dance, theatre, cinema, literature and heritage walks - is Mumbai's most celebrated cultural event, drawing hundreds of thousands of visitors every February. Fort without Kala Ghoda would be like Paris without the Left Bank.

best_services.name: Living and Working in Fort
best_services.description: Fort is primarily a commercial and institutional district - its daytime population of hundreds of thousands dwarfs its small residential community. But those who do live in Fort - the Parsi families in their heritage buildings, the advocates with chambers and homes within walking distance of the High Court, the artists and gallery owners of Kala Ghoda - would not trade their address for anything in Mumbai. The connectivity is unmatched: CST and Churchgate within walking distance, Metro Line 3 at CST, BEST buses covering every corner of the city. The food is legendary: Britannia & Co. in Ballard Estate, the Irani cafés near Flora Fountain, the Kala Ghoda café scene. And the sheer beauty of the built environment - the Victorian Gothic spires, the Art Deco facades, the wide boulevards of Ballard Estate - makes Fort one of the most extraordinary places to live and work in the world.
